rows.name: multipart-pause-1500
rows.question: For exactly ten thousand elements and one hundred ninety two threads per block, compute the minimum number of blocks needed to cover every element. Also report the active threads in the final block and the number of launched threads that need a bounds check. Explain the arithmetic.
rows.recognizedQuestion: For example, ten thousand elements and one hundred ninety two threads per block compute the minimum number of blocks needed to cover every element Also report the active threads in the final block and the number of launched threads that need a bounce check Explain the arithmetic
rows.answer: You need 53 blocks, with 16 active threads in the final block. Since 52 × 192 = 9,984, that leaves 10,000 − 9,984 = 16 elements, requiring one more block. Launching 53 × 192 = 10,176 threads gives 176 excess threads; interpreting “bounce check” as “bounds check,” every thread should check index < 10,000, and those 176 threads must skip the work.

rows.name: switch-topic
rows.question: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.recognizedQuestion: Switch topics. Why does snapshot isolation permit write skew even if both read-check-write sequences run in atomic transactions?
rows.answer:
Snapshot isolation makes each transaction atomic, but it does not make concurrent transactions equivalent to running one after the other. Both can read the same old snapshot, pass a check, and update different rows, so there is no write-write conflict to prevent both commits.

For example, the rule is that at least one of two doctors must remain on call. Each transaction sees both doctors on call and takes a different doctor off call; both commit, leaving neither on call. Atomicity prevents partial transactions, not this cross-transaction violation; serializable isolation or suitable locking can prevent it.

review.note: Correctly distinguishes transaction atomicity from serializability, explains disjoint writes, gives the two-doctor counterexample and a suitable serializable/locking remedy.
review.usefulPrefix: Snapshot isolation makes each transaction atomic, but it does not make concurrent transactions equivalent to running one after the other.
